text.en: Meena read about India's neighbours on a map. "Who are our neighbours?" she asked.

India has several neighbours: Pakistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Sri Lanka and the Maldives. Relations include trade, culture and sometimes border disputes. India works for peaceful solutions.
SAARC, formed in 1985, is the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation. India also joins groups like BRICS, the G20 and the Commonwealth, and plays a role in the UN, including in peacekeeping.
India's relations with big powers like the USA, Russia and the European Union matter for trade, defence and technology. India also helps other countries through aid and education.

A nation never thrives alone: geography gives India seven land neighbours and maritime neighbours across the Indian Ocean, making regional cooperation vital.
Let us tour our immediate neighbourhood. With Nepal and Bhutan, India enjoys open borders, friendship treaties and shared Himalayan hydropower and pilgrim circuits.
With Bangladesh—whose independence India supported in 1971—cooperation covers the Ganga water treaty, cross-border trains and the Land Boundary Agreement.
With Sri Lanka across the Palk Strait and Maldives across the Arabian Sea, India partners on ferry links, maritime security and clean drinking water.

board.text: Sri Lanka & Maldives: sea neighbours & aid

text.en: With Myanmar—India's land bridge to Southeast Asia—projects like the Kaladan multimodal corridor link India's Northeast to Bay of Bengal ports.

board.text: Myanmar: India's land gateway to ASEAN

text.en: With China and Pakistan, relations combine diplomacy, trade and efforts to manage sensitive Himalayan boundary and cross-border security challenges peacefully.
Think of shared history: ancient trade along the Silk Road, Spice Routes, and Buddhism travelling from India to Sri Lanka, East and Southeast Asia built cultural kinship.

board.text: Ancient cultural & trade links across Asia

text.en: Since 1985, SAARC—bringing eight South Asian nations together with its Secretariat in Kathmandu—aimed at regional agriculture, health and SAFTA trade.
Alongside SAARC, BIMSTEC connects seven Bay of Bengal nations—Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Thailand—bridging South and Southeast Asia.
Look further at major powers: with the USA, India partners on space, semiconductors, higher education, clean energy and defence technology.
With Russia—a long-standing partner since the 1971 Treaty of Peace—cooperation spans Bhilai steel plants, nuclear power at Kudankulam and spaceflight.
With Japan, high-speed rail, metro lines in Chennai and Delhi, and quality infrastructure transform Indian cities cleanly.
With the European Union, West Asia and Africa, India trades pharmaceuticals, engineering goods, software, solar projects and scholarships.
Globally, BRICS—originally Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa—created the New Development Bank to finance infrastructure in developing nations.
Inside the G20, India hosted the historic 2023 New Delhi Summit, welcoming the African Union as a permanent member for inclusive global governance.
Inside the United Nations, India is a founding member advocating Security Council reform so developing countries gain fair permanent representation.

board.text: India urges UN Security Council reform

text.en: Over two lakh Indian peacekeepers have served in UN Blue Helmet missions in Congo, Korea, Lebanon and South Sudan, earning global respect.

board.text: Indian Blue Helmets lead UN peacekeeping

text.en: Even the International Solar Alliance—headquartered in Gurugram—unites over 100 sunny nations co-founded by India and France to cut fossil fuels.

board.text: International Solar Alliance for clean power

text.en: Remember cultural soft power too: International Day of Yoga, Ayurveda and Indian cinema connect peoples beyond government treaties.
Why does multi-forum diplomacy work? No single bloc solves climate change, pandemics or trade supply chains alone.

board.text: Shared global problems need shared forums

text.en: Compare regional vs global bodies cleanly: SAARC and BIMSTEC focus on neighbours, while BRICS, G20 and the UN tackle planetary issues.
To connect the whole chapter: friendly neighbours -> strong Asian corridors -> balanced global partnerships -> fairer UN & green world.
Through patient dialogue, technology sharing and peacekeeping, India builds friendships rooted in respect and shared growth.

board.text: International ties turn neighbours into partners

problem.en: Why does India participate in both regional groups like BIMSTEC/SAARC and global forums like BRICS and G20?

text.en: Spot regional needs.

why.en: Borders, cross-border rivers, cyclone warnings and regional railways require direct cooperation with South and Southeast Asian neighbours via SAARC and BIMSTEC.

text.en: Spot global challenges.

why.en: Climate finance, global trade rules, digital governance and UN Security Council reform involve major economies across continents.

text.en: Combine both tracks.

why.en: Working regionally keeps borders peaceful and trade moving, while global forums let India voice Global South priorities alongside major powers.

prompt.en: A friend says India has no neighbours. How will you reply?
